In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the membrane-associated and cytoplasmic folate-binding proteins of KB cells are different proteins, but that they are similar in their folate-binding properties.
the soluble folate receptor is a truncated form of the membrane-associated receptor.

the membrane-associated and secreted folate-binding proteins of human KB cells are structurally and functionally similar, but the membrane-associated folate binding protein is a more efficient transporter for physiologic folate derivatives and is a more efficient binder of methotrexates than is the soluble folate binding protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that

the membrane-associated folate- binding protein is a 45,000-dalton integral membrane protein that is important in cellular folate accumulation and methotrexate transport, and the soluble folates-binding protein is a 24,000-dal-ton glycoprotein that is released by the cell and is important in the transport and metabolism of folate.
the membrane-associated and cytosolic folate-binding proteins of KB cells have similar properties and may be derived from the same gene.

KB cells contain two folate-binding proteins which are similar in their amino acid content, their carbohydrate content, and their affinity for folates and methotrexate, but which differ in their size and in their subcellular distribution.
The main takeaway from our work is that
there are multiple folate-binding proteins in KB cells.

the membrane-associated folate- binding protein is the primary folate transporter in KB cells, and the soluble folates- binding protein may be a degradation product of the membrane-associated protein.
there are two distinct species of folate-binding proteins in KB cells, and that both proteins bind polyglutamylated methotrexate.
